standard.title: Scientific Knowledge Used by Communities
standard.description: investigate how scientific knowledge is used by individuals and communities to identify problems, consider responses and make decisions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can examine how scientific explanations are used to meet needs or solve problems (AC9S3H02, 3-4 band). They now extend to examining how knowledge is used by communities — not just to design solutions, but to identify problems, evaluate responses and make collective decisions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate examples where scientific knowledge enables individuals and communities to identify problems, evaluate possible responses and make decisions — examining what knowledge was used, what options were considered, and how decisions were reached.

nodes.label: Scientific knowledge helps identify and define problems
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how scientific knowledge enables people to identify and precisely define a problem — distinguishing between a symptom (what is observed) and a cause (what the knowledge explains).
nodes.minimum_width: Students describe one example where scientific knowledge helped identify a problem, explaining what the knowledge was and how it enabled the problem to be recognised.
nodes.typical_width: Students examine how knowledge of erosion processes enables identification of at-risk landscapes, and how knowledge of light properties enables identification of light pollution as a problem — explaining in each case how scientific knowledge transforms an observable phenomenon into a defined problem with a cause.
wider: Examine how park rangers use knowledge of erosion to identify and define problems in fragile environments — distinguishing natural and human-caused erosion and predicting risk locations
Investigate how knowledge of light pollution and its effects on ecosystems enables communities to identify artificial lighting as a problem requiring management
Research how First Nations Australians use ecological knowledge to identify problems in Country — examining how deep observational knowledge enables early problem recognition
success_criteria: Describes one example where scientific knowledge enabled a problem to be identified
Explains what the knowledge was and how it transformed an observation into a defined problem with a cause

nodes.label: Scientific knowledge informs decisions and responses
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can examine how communities use scientific knowledge to evaluate options and make decisions — explaining what knowledge was used, what options were considered, and why a particular response was chosen.
nodes.minimum_width: Students describe one example where a community used scientific knowledge to make a decision, identifying the knowledge used and the decision made.
nodes.typical_width: Students examine multiple examples where communities use scientific knowledge to make decisions — farming decisions based on habitat knowledge, erosion mitigation design, light pollution reduction strategies — explaining the knowledge-to-decision pathway and evaluating the trade-offs involved.
wider: Research how communities have used knowledge of light pollution to design and implement solutions — covered streetlights, automated systems, motion sensors — and evaluate each response's effectiveness
Examine how people use properties of light to design signal lamps for Morse code communication — tracing the knowledge-to-application pathway for a historical and ongoing technology

Consider how communities in different regions make decisions about which crops or animals to farm based on local habitat conditions — examining how biological knowledge shapes agricultural decision-making

response_modes.reason: Students tend to see science as producing one correct answer rather than informing a decision among multiple options. Encountering varied decision contexts — where different communities make different but scientifically informed choices — builds a more accurate model of how scientific knowledge functions in community decision-making.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Light pollution community responses provide a rich, elaboration-grounded direction where scientific knowledge directly shapes infrastructure and policy decisions. The agricultural decision direction connects biological knowledge to everyday economic choices.
success_criteria: Describes one example where a community used scientific knowledge to make a decision
Explains what knowledge was used, what options were considered, and why the chosen response was selected
